transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in?

Um... mostly just work stuff, I guess. I can't really keep my mind on the actual experiment anymore. 

If I'm on a grant call, or in a safety meeting... I'll notice a pump vibration in the lab, or maybe a student makes a side comment, or I'll remember some odd peak in an old spectrum. And I just... I end up off chasing that for hours. While the thing everyone actually needs from me just sort of falls apart.
Have you ever had a period when you felt unusually energized and needed much less sleep than usual?

I suppose. Um... most nights I only get about two or three hours. I usually just end up on the couch with my laptop still open. 

But I don't feel tired. I actually wake up pretty sharp, ready to get back to work. It just... sleep feels like an inefficient interruption right now, I guess.
During these times when you sleep only a few hours, do you feel unusually upbeat or euphoric?

Euphoric is... I don't know. I wouldn't really use that word. It’s more just that, for months now, it feels like the lab is finally moving at my speed. Everything just feels... electrified, almost. 

But I wouldn't say I'm always upbeat. If someone questions my plan, or... or tells me to slow down, I... well, I tend to snap at them. I think it's gotten to the point where... some of the students are just avoiding my office entirely.
Have you been taking on a lot more projects or work than usual lately?

I suppose. Um... I've been getting to the lab before anyone else arrives. Just... rewriting protocols, mostly. Rearranging the instrument schedules. 

I've also been emailing some collaborators in... three different countries, I think. Trying to get a bunch of new analyses started all at once. It's just... if I sit still right now, it feels like I'm wasting the one chance I have to actually fix everything. So... yes, I guess I'm doing more.
Have there been times when this very high-energy, little-sleep state was clearly not your usual self?
I don't really know what you mean by "not my usual self." I mean... I've always been driven. The work is important. It's just... more intense right now. I'm just trying to get things done.
When you sleep only two or three hours, do you still feel fully rested the next day?

Yes. I don't wake up tired, if that's what you mean. 

Most nights it's just... two or three hours. Sometimes I just stay on the couch, you know, with my laptop still open. But when I wake up, I'm sharp. I'm ready to work. Honestly, sleep just feels like an inefficient interruption right now.
Lately, have you felt more confident or capable than usual—like you can accomplish things other people couldn't?

I suppose so. I mean... the multi-site project was failing, and I just knew I could fix it. 

I figured out how to redesign the whole spectroscopy approach by myself. And... I realized I could probably mentor all the grad students better than their actual advisors do. It's just... I know I can beat the grant deadline, if people would just stop getting in my way and slowing me down. So, yes, I guess I feel capable.
During this high-energy period, have you done anything unusually risky or impulsive for you?
No. I don't... I wouldn't say that. I'm just focused on getting the work done.
Do you feel more important or gifted than usual right now?

I... I thought I just answered that. I don't know about the word "gifted." 

It's just... I know I'm the only one who can actually rescue this whole project by myself. Like I said, I'm the one redesigning the spectroscopy approach. And I have to step in for the advisors because I can obviously mentor their students better than they can. It's just facts. I can hit the grant deadline if everyone would just... stop getting in my way. 

I don't know if that makes me feel "important." It just means I'm the only one who can actually do it.
Has this high-energy period caused serious problems at work or in your relationships?

I mean... I wouldn't call them serious problems. 

There's been some... friction, I guess. The department head stepped in recently. They took over some of the decisions I usually handle. Said something about missed priorities and... scheduling issues. They claimed my supervision of the grad students was getting strained, and that it was putting the project at risk. Even brought up lab safety expectations, which is ridiculous. 

But I wouldn't say it's a serious problem. They just don't understand my process right now.
Before this recent period, was there a clear stretch of time when you felt like your usual self?
I... I don't really know what you mean by that. I guess so. I mean, I was just working like normal before all this... before the deadline got closer. I was just doing my job.
How long has this high-energy, little-sleep period been going on without really letting up?
I don't know... a while, I guess. It's been about seven months. Ever since I took over the multi-site spectroscopy project.
